## Intent
Hypothesis: fusing the scatter-reduction render into the step loop eliminates intermediate-buffer traffic, keeping the working set cache-resident and approaching the streaming ceiling.

## Cache saturation
The ns/particle curve is FLAT across N at every death rate, with no knee at any cache boundary. At q=0.01, cost holds at 26.057 ns/p at N=10000 (just past the L2 spill at N≈7710) and drops slightly to 24.239 ns/p at N=10000000 (far past the L3 spill at N≈246723). The L1d spill (N≈481) and L2 spill (N≈7710) produce no penalty; the 68·N working set transitions through L1, L2, L3, and DRAM without rising cost. Death rate raises the floor monotonically — 25→27→29.8→34.9 ns/p as q goes 0.01→0.1→0.25→0.5 — without changing the flat N-shape, indicating respawn adds per-particle overhead without introducing cache sensitivity. The absence of any spill knee supports the cache-residency claim.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved bandwidth is 2.81 GB/s at N=10000000, q=0.01 — 22% of the 12.69 GB/s streaming ceiling. The algo is overhead-bound, not bandwidth-bound: frontend stalls dominate at 65.3–67.1% across all configurations, with backend stalls at 0.0% and branch flushes at 0.0%. Bandwidth never transitions to bandwidth-bound at any N or death rate. Rising death rate erodes achieved bandwidth (2.81→2.57→2.29→1.95 GB/s at N=10M as q goes 0.01→0.5), tracking respawn cost rather than any memory-system limit.

## Assembly
The compiler vectorized component-wise within one particle, not across particles. The integration uses `vmovups xmm0,[r12]` to load 4 floats, then `vmulps`/`vaddps`/`vshufps`/`vinsertps` for packed 4-wide position updates. No gather appears; particle data is accessed sequentially at stride 0x44 (68 bytes). The framebuffer scatter is entirely byte-granular: `movzx r11d,BYTE PTR [r13+r9*1+0x0]`, `add`, `cmp bx,0xff`, `cmovae`, `mov BYTE PTR [r13+r9*1+0x0],bl` — a load-add-saturate-store chain repeated for 3 channels across up to 4 pixel positions per particle. These scalar byte RMW sequences (28 `movzx`, 27 `cmp`, 12 `cmovae`) dominate the 343-instruction body and explain the 65%+ frontend stall: the instruction stream is too long and serial to keep the core fed, capping bandwidth at 22% of ceiling.

## Verdict
Refuted — the fused scatter-reduction never exceeds 2.81 GB/s (22% of the 12.69 GB/s ceiling) at N=10000000, q=0.01, falling to 1.95 GB/s at q=0.5. The flat N-curve confirms no cache-spill penalty from eliminating intermediates, but the 65%+ frontend stalls and 343-instruction step body — dominated by byte-granular framebuffer scatter (`movzx`/`add`/`cmp`/`cmovae`/`mov` per channel per pixel) — prevent approaching the streaming ceiling. Fusing eliminated cache pressure but not instruction overhead.
